---
title: "Building and maintaining the documentation"
---

All documentation sources in docs/ use Quarto .qmd, including executable
estimator walkthroughs. The root README.md remains a short repository entry
point. docs/_quarto.yml defines a searchable HTML website with navigation,
mathematical notation, code and results. Quarto builds into the gitignored
docs/_site/ directory. `scripts/render-docs` copies the rendered website into
docs/ alongside the .qmd sources, including docs/index.html and required assets.
The statistical engine does not depend on Quarto.

## Render or preview saved results

Install the [Quarto CLI](https://quarto.org/docs/download/) for your platform.
On macOS, `brew install --cask quarto` is also available. Check `quarto --version`;
this project was rendered with Quarto 1.10.18.

From the repository root:

```sh
quarto render docs
quarto preview docs
```

The website reuses saved computations in docs/_freeze/. Keep this directory in
version control: a complete website render does not require Python, R, or a built
PHP extension when those saved results are present. The JSON comparison report,
reference fixtures and executable source code are also retained in the repository.
Generated HTML/assets are checked in for GitHub Pages; .qmd files remain
the editable sources. Quarto's local .quarto/ state stays gitignored.

A render that reuses saved outputs is a presentation check, not a fresh numerical
verification. The walkthroughs show versions from their last execution. Quarto's
[freeze documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/code-execution.html)
explains why incremental file renders execute code even when a project-wide
render reuses outputs.

## Recompute the walkthroughs

Follow [development setup](development.qmd) to select matching PHP and headers,
and install R with Rscript available. The mixed-model reference also requires
R's lme4 package, plus nlme for the published-data comparison. These are
development dependencies rather than PHP runtime dependencies:

```sh
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("lme4", "nlme"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'
```

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -m venv .context/notebooks-venv
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/pip install -r docs/notebooks/requirements.txt
export QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python"
# macOS development installation; select matching paths on your platform.
export PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php
export PHP_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/bin/php-config
cargo build -p phit --locked
export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib"
# Linux: use libphit.so and matching PHP/PHP_CONFIG paths.
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_ols.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-public-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/data/lmm/index.qmd
quarto render docs/benchmarks/lmm.qmd
quarto render docs
```

The individual page renders execute their code and refresh the saved outputs;
the final full render assembles the website. RSCRIPT can select a non-default
Rscript executable. QUARTO_PYTHON selects the virtual environment without adding
machine-specific paths to the project configuration. Review changes to .qmd,
_freeze/ and verifications/ols-results.json together. Input-data or estimator
changes require re-execution even if the prose has not changed.

## Recompute each model's notebooks

With the environment above, each estimator's comparison script and notebooks
run in this order:

```sh
export QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python"
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_ols.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-verification.qmd
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_logistic.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/logistic-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/logistic-verification.qmd
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_probit.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_poisson.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/probit-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/probit-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/poisson-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/poisson-verification.qmd
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_lmm.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-verification.qmd
quarto render docs
```

The individual page renders execute all chunks in order and update _freeze/.
Review source, output and comparison-report diffs when regenerating. Outputs record
evidence from the environment used, not a guarantee for every platform. The
verification scripts capture PHP warnings to keep JSON output valid, then show
and check those warnings explicitly. Use a Quarto-compatible editor for interactive
.qmd authoring; generated .ipynb files are not the maintained source.

## Writing a walkthrough

Each implemented estimator has an executable walkthrough. Do not create
placeholder notebooks for methods phit does not implement.

Use a small reproducible simulated dataset with named variables, units, noise,
and meaningful relationships. State its generating equation, seed, population
parameters, and observed sample correlations. Save and share the actual observations;
label them synthetic and explain that correlation alone is not causation.
See the [learning-data convention](design-philosophy.qmd#learning-examples-use-meaningful-simulated-data).
State the model assumptions and input ordering,
derive the calculations before displaying them, connect fields to production code,
and explain edge cases. Supply equivalent R, statsmodels and PHP calls when those
references support the estimator. State any differences in statistical conventions
rather than silently adapting one library's results. Keep assertions near the
results and preserve executed outputs. Share inputs with reference tests where
possible; avoid three separate datasets that only look similar.

## Authoring and verification

Edit .qmd files directly. Ordinary fenced blocks such as `python`, `r` and `php`
are displayed examples; `{python}` chunks execute in the Jupyter kernel. Both OLS
walkthroughs use Python chunks, with the comparison runner invoking R and PHP.
Execution starts in docs/ and the code discovers the repository root by locating
Cargo.toml. A missing dependency or failed assertion must fail the render.

Use relative links to .qmd pages so Quarto rewrites them to HTML links. Keep local
reference data and scripts alongside the verification document. Each future
implemented estimator should have a derivation walkthrough and equivalent-model
verification evidence, following [the notebook guide](notebooks/index.qmd).

For prose-only pages, render the site and check navigation and local links. Any
edit to a computational walkthrough (including prose) requires an individual page
render to update its frozen content. For computational edits, rerun the affected pages and comparison scripts, inspect
output, and run the appropriate [Rust/PHP checks](verification.qmd). Saved
results must never be mistaken for a new estimator test run.

## Standard figures

All benchmark and notebook figures use the shared R/ggplot2 strategy in
[Figure conventions](visualization.qmd). SVG/PNG exports, fixed language ordering,
colors/shapes, units, scale choices and input/package provenance use the same
renderer. Python remains a numerical/verification notebook engine rather than a
second drawing implementation. Matplotlib is not a documentation dependency.

To refresh saved figures without estimating or timing anything:

```sh
Rscript docs/figures/render.R --all
./scripts/render-docs
```

The renderer uses saved reports and small notebook-exported point snapshots.
Individual .qmd execution invokes the R renderer when appropriate. Saved images
and frozen outputs support browsing/rendering without rerunning scientific checks.

## Publish

phpstats.org imports the rendered HTML committed under `docs/`, and GitHub
Pages serves the same directory at <https://phpstats.github.io/phit/>. Neither
runs Quarto. The site's navigation is the sidebar in `docs/_quarto.yml`, so
every page listed there needs its rendered HTML committed. After editing .qmd
sources or refreshing frozen results, run:

```sh
./scripts/render-docs
```

Commit the regenerated HTML/assets with their sources and push to main.
`docs/.nojekyll` lets GitHub Pages serve the static Quarto website directly,
including asset directories containing underscores. `quarto render docs` alone
writes only `docs/_site/`; the script also copies the result into `docs/`.
